newsitem.title: GERMANY: German "wise man" says don't rule out EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German "wise man" says don't rule out EMU delay.

text.p: German economist Juergen Donges, was quoted on Sunday as saying Chancellor Helmut Kohl should not rule out delaying the planned 1999 start to European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"A later start is possible. History will not judge whether we started monetary union at a specific point in time, rather whether we started it well," Donges told Focus magazine in an interview released ahead of publication on Monday.

Donges, one of a panel of economic advisors to Kohl's government known as the five wise men, said the fear that a delay to the single currency would lead to a sharp appreciation in the deutschemark was unfounded.
"That would only be plausible if the current value of the D-mark on the finance markets was in anticipation of the euro, because the markets didn't believe in the euro's stability.
"But that would just be a sign that Europe was not ready for a joint, stable curency," he said.

Donges said he did not think Germany could hit the EMU deficit entry criterion of three percent to gross domestic product precisely without accounting tricks, but said it was important this target was reached before the euro began.

"The example of France shows how quickly 3.1 can become 3.6 or 3.8," he said. "There must be a fixed point. A judge does not accept it if a driver just exceeds the alcohol limit and says 'but it was only half a glass of beer over'."
